findings.text: The pattern-mood AI trader leads to date: 60 trades, 31 wins, net 12870.63 INR, return 0.21%; this week 9 trades, 6 wins, net 1666.29. It reads prices, regime and sectors only. 60 trades is a small sample and these inputs carry no luck test, so this is not yet evidence of skill.

Both baselines lose after costs to date: always-buy 1006 trades, 437 wins, -0.02%; follow-yesterday 515 trades, 207 wins, -0.11%. Their week swung with the market: baselines lost 84819.77 in Monday's settlements and gained 88973.14 in Friday's. A strategy must beat these yardsticks before its result means anything.

News-led strategies trail: the news-and-results AI trader has 8 trades, 1 win, net -11410.73 (-1.43%); the double-news rule has 15 trades, 3 wins, net -12192.9 (-0.81%). With 8 and 15 trades this cannot separate poor use of news from bad luck. The other rule strategies and both combined AI traders do not appear in the leaders tables.

Verified news cannot be judged yet: the confirmed_primary and corroborated earnings and analyst rows are all 'not enough events yet' (at most 4 events). The statuses the signal model weights most therefore have no measured effect this week; these rows are not evidence either way.

Single-source medium analyst news shows positive abnormal returns at 3 and 4 days (+1.08%, CI 0.57 to 1.60; +1.37%, CI 0.75 to 1.99), but mean sector moves of 2.86% and 4.17% suggest sector rallies may be mixed in. Single-source high earnings news flips sign: -0.46% at 2 days, +0.72% at 3. One week only: likely noise.

In the cited trade reasons, the DRREDDY win is put down to a sector lift with no news part, while the HDFCBANK miss is the largest news-led miss (reason code news_negative). The daily review notes targets were reached in session 1 on most items, yet several trades still ended with large losses.
